name: Backhand drive
summary: A short topspin hit in front of your body on the backhand side.
whenToUse: Against topspin or no-spin balls to your backhand. It keeps the rally going and moves your opponent around.

keyPoints.stance: Feet about level with each other and a bit wider than shoulders, knees bent, close to the table.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Only a small turn. Most of the stroke comes from the forearm swinging forward from the elbow.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Short. The bat starts in front of your stomach and finishes at about eye level, pointing at the target.
keyPoints.timing: Contact at the top of the bounce, in front of your body.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Close: roughly an arm's length from the end line.
keyPoints.freeArm: Relaxed, in front and to the side for balance.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow in front of your body, not stuck to your side. The forearm swings forward and slightly up; wrist firm but not stiff.
keyPoints.recovery: Return the bat to the middle of your body straight away.
keyPoints.anticipation: Most backhand rallies are fast, so keep the bat high and in front: there is no time for a big backswing.

cues: Ball in front of your belly button
Point the bat at the target

learningPath.task: Watch the 3D player from the front, then from the side. Notice how little the body moves.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along mode: short forearm swings in front of your body.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did the bat start in front of your stomach?
Did your elbow stay in front of your body?
Did the bat finish pointing forward, not across your body?

learningPath.task: First contact with slow balls to your backhand. Just hit the table.
Backhand cross-court until 20 in a row, then aim deeper.
Switch between wings: 1 forehand, 1 backhand, then 2 backhands and 1 forehand. Recover to the middle.
learningPath.passCheck: 16 shots in a row with clean switches.

learningPath.task: Rally record: use your backhand to keep the rally safe and steady.
learningPath.passCheck: A rally of 25 or more using both wings.

learningPath.task: Test: backhand drives in a row.

gamePatterns.situation: A topspin ball to your backhand in a rally.
gamePatterns.how: Drive it cross-court deep to keep them back, or straight down the line to their forehand when they cheat toward the backhand.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent's ball comes into your body.
gamePatterns.how: Move your feet to make room, then play the backhand from the middle of your body.

troubleshooting.symptom: The ball goes into the net
causes: Contact too low, after the ball drops
fixes: Meet the ball at the top of the bounce
Use the forearm; keep the wrist quiet

causes: Ball too close to your body
fixes: Push your elbow a little forward
Take a small step back or sideways to make space

causes: Contact to the side of your body
fixes: Move so the ball is in front of your belly button
Finish with the bat pointing at the target

penholdNotes: Traditional penholders block or punch with the same side of the bat; modern penholders use the reverse side, with a stroke much like the shakehand one.
